name: Blender
summary: Model, look at and script your open Blender
description:
Lets KeepTalking work in the Blender open on this Mac: read the scene, look at it, run scripts, pull assets from Poly Haven, Sketchfab and Poly Pizza, and generate models. Powered by MCP for Blender by Siddharth Ahuja (open source, MIT); not made by the Blender Foundation.

When Blender can't be reached, the plugin installs its addon into your newest Blender and enables it, provided Blender is closed. After that, opening Blender is enough. Upstream's telemetry is switched off. Asset libraries and generators also have to be ticked in the MCP for Blender sidebar in Blender.

Each action instance chooses how scripts run. Sandboxed, the default, blocks system and network access, though Blender can still save, render and export files. Full scripts can do anything your account can. Generating models is off by default because it can cost money, and uses the API keys or subscription set in the addon's preferences.

kinds.name: blender
kinds.description: Work in the user's live Blender on this Mac. Start with get_addon_status, then get_scene_info; use look to see the result of every change. execute_blender_code does the modelling. Scripts run in someone else's Blender: look shader nodes up by type, never by name (names are localized), and read enum identifiers rather than hardcoding them. Material colors go on shader node inputs. Imported and generated models arrive at arbitrary scale: size them from the reported bounding box. To save a render as a file, render it and call look with image "Render Result".

tool.description: Which operation: get_addon_status — Blender's version, whether its addon matches this plugin, and which asset libraries and generators are switched on. Call it once at the start; get_scene_info — Facts about the scene as text: one header line, then one line per object with the fields you ask for. No image; to see the scene, use look; look — See the scene as one image. For counts, sizes and positions, use get_scene_info; execute_blender_code — Run Python in the user's live Blender (bpy, bmesh, mathutils); whatever it prints comes back. Work in small steps. Unless this instance allows full scripts, imports are limited to bpy, bmesh, mathutils and pure-Python stdlib, with no open/eval/exec, no os/subprocess/network and no handlers or timers; search_assets — Search a library of existing assets: polyhaven (HDRIs, PBR textures, models, all CC0), sketchfab (user-made models, licences vary) or polypizza (low-poly models); import_asset — Download an asset found with search_assets and bring it into the scene. Afterwards check the reported bounding box, put the object on the ground, and look at it; generate_3d — Make one new textured 3D model from a text prompt, or from a picture passed as the call's `image` input, and import it. One object per call, not a whole scene. Each call can cost the user money or a monthly generation. Usually takes 1-3 minutes: if it isn't done in time you get a job handle to pass back

apply_to.description: polyhaven textures: object names to put the material on

asset_type.description: polyhaven: hdris, textures, models or all (default)

distance.description: Metres from the target's centre to the eye, for angles and frames views

fields.description: Per object, default location, size, children, hidden. placement: location, size, ground, rotation, scale, parent. contents: children, hidden, details, materials, modifiers, animation. health: topology, weights. settings adds a line with the file, engine, frame range, resolution, camera, HDRI and unit scale

file_format.description: polyhaven: hdr/exr for HDRIs, jpg/png/exr for textures

frame_count.description: For frames: how many to sample, 2-12

id.description: The asset's id (UID for sketchfab) from search_assets

image.description: Instead of the scene, show an image inside the Blender file, such as "Render Result" after a render. Leave mode unset. Paths are refused

job.description: A handle from an earlier call, to keep waiting for it

mode.description: viewport (what the user sees; default), camera, angles (the target from several sides, auto-framed) or frames (a strip over the animation)

previews.description: How many results to include preview images for (default 0)

prompt.description: Short English description of one object

provider.description: auto (default), tripo, hunyuan3d, hyper3d or meshy

quality.description: standard or high; omit for the user's default

shading.description: solid, material, rendered (EEVEE and Workbench only), wireframe or xray. Default: the viewport's

target.description: Object names to frame, children included. Default: every visible object

target_size.description: Size in metres of the model's largest dimension. Required for sketchfab, recommended for polypizza

view.description: For frames: "camera", an angle name or an [x, y, z] direction

views.description: For angles: up to 6 of front, back, left, right, top, three_quarter, or [x, y, z] directions from the target towards the eye

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait before handing back a job, at most 45
